code.originalText: Review three weeks after cytoreductive surgery: pathology, genetic results, and the first cycle of chemotherapy

text.paragraph: Review three weeks after cytoreductive surgery, on the first chemotherapy day. [S]

Ms. Radner returns three weeks after primary cytoreductive surgery: hysterectomy with removal of both tubes and ovaries, total omentectomy, stripping of the right diaphragm, and excision of pelvic nodules, with no visible disease left. She went home on the fifth day. The wound has healed. She is giving herself enoxaparin each evening and will finish the 28 days next week; she has had no bleeding or leg swelling. She needed acetaminophen for two weeks and nothing now. Her appetite is back and the bloating has gone. Since surgery she has hot flashes several times a day and night sweats. She came this morning for her first cycle of carboplatin and paclitaxel. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1986-05-12; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 112/70, pulse 84; weight 55.2 kg
Midline incision healed without redness or hernia; soft, non-tender; no fluid
Light touch, pinprick and vibration normal in the hands and feet; ankle reflexes present (baseline before paclitaxel)
No calf tenderness or swelling; injection sites on the abdomen clean

Persistent bloating with tightness of her clothes, feeling full after a few bites, a dull lower abdominal and pelvic ache, and passing urine more often, on most days for about four weeks, in a woman of 39: the ovarian cancer symptom index is positive. Examination: a distended abdomen with shifting dullness and a firm, fixed, irregular mass in the right adnexa. Suspected ovarian cancer; transvaginal ultrasound, CT, CA-125 and gynecologic oncology review booked within the week
S — Synthetic presenting problem linked to her documented abdominal symptoms; superseded by the diagnosis at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

High-grade serous carcinoma of both ovaries (Mullerian origin), diagnosed by image-guided omental core biopsy (PAX8 and WT1 positive, p53 aberrant), with bilateral adnexal masses, ascites, omental and diaphragmatic disease on CT: clinical FIGO stage IIIC; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented ovarian cancer
S — Synthetic histology and stage; the documented diagnosis was stage IV ovarian cancer (D).
Peritoneal and omental metastases of the ovarian cancer, with ascites

list.item:
High-grade serous carcinoma of both ovaries, FIGO stage IIIC, after complete gross resection (C56.3). Surgery achieved the best outcome, no visible residual disease. Pathology confirms stage IIIC. The germline panel is negative, so there is no inherited variant to pass on; the tumor carries a BRCA1 pathogenic variant that arose in the tumor and is homologous recombination deficient. If she responds to chemotherapy, maintenance with a PARP inhibitor is recommended. CA-125 has fallen from 1240 to 188. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests were negative. Blood counts, kidney and liver function, and magnesium allow full-dose treatment: creatinine 0.68 mg/dL, estimated creatinine clearance about 97 mL/min. [S]
Cycle 1 of carboplatin AUC 5 (610 mg) and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 (275 mg) today, every 21 days for six cycles.
Fosaprepitant, palonosetron and dexamethasone before each cycle; ondansetron at home as needed.
Temperature twice a day for a week after each cycle; call at once for 38.0 °C or more.
Finish enoxaparin next week.

Family history of ovarian cancer (Z80.41). Her own germline result is negative. The genetic counselor advised that, because three relatives had ovarian cancer and none was tested, her blood relatives may still benefit from their own genetic counseling; a negative result in her does not rule out an inherited cause in the family. [S]
Copy of the result and the counselor's letter for her to share as she chooses.

Symptomatic surgical menopause (E89.41). Hot flashes and night sweats since both ovaries were removed at 39. Hormone therapy is not ruled out by high-grade serous cancer and will be discussed at the end of treatment; for now non-hormonal measures. [S]
Layered clothing, a fan, and cooling bedding.
Revisit at each visit; bone density scan after treatment.
